sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: Headroom compresses what an AI agent or app sends to a language model (tool outputs, logs, retrieved chunks, files and chat history) before it reaches the model. It runs on your machine as a Python or TypeScript library, a local proxy, or a wrapper around coding agents like Claude Code and Codex.
sixtySeconds.problem: Agents pay for every input token, and much of what they read is repetitive JSON, logs and file contents. Headroom shrinks that content locally and keeps the originals so the model can fetch the full text when it needs it.
whoFor: Developers paying for LLM input tokens in their apps
Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and Copilot users
Teams building agents with LangChain, LiteLLM, Agno or Strands
Anyone wanting local, private prompt compression
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it to cut input tokens with no code changes for coding agents, or one function call in your own app. The README reports 21 to 57% fewer input tokens across four agent scenarios and little gain on plain prose.
requirements: An existing LLM app or coding agent

overview: Headroom works four ways: a compress() function you call in Python or TypeScript, a proxy you run on port 8787 with no code changes, a wrap command that launches a coding agent through the proxy, and an MCP server with compress, retrieve and stats tools.

Inside, a content router detects whether text is JSON, source code or prose and picks a compressor for each. A cache aligner flags content that would break a provider's prompt cache, and CCR keeps originals locally so the model can call headroom_retrieve for the full text. Compression runs on your machine; the README says no prompt or file content is sent anywhere to be compressed.

Extras include cross-agent memory shared by Claude, Codex, Gemini and Grok, headroom learn (which mines failed sessions and writes corrections to files like CLAUDE.local.md) and output token reduction. Headroom Enterprise is a separate commercial offering; this repository stays Apache-2.0.

features.title: Proxy
features.body: Drop-in local proxy for any OpenAI-compatible client.

features.title: Agent wrap
features.body: One command for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot, Aider and more.

features.title: Reversible
features.body: Originals cached locally and retrievable on demand.

features.title: MCP server
features.body: Compress, retrieve and stats tools for MCP clients.

features.title: Cross-agent memory
features.body: One shared memory store across agents.

strengths: Runs locally; content isn't sent out to be compressed
No code changes needed for coding agents
Measured savings published in the README
limitations: Savings are small on plain prose
headroom wrap's proxy only lives as long as the wrapped session
Adds another moving part between your app and the provider

install.verificationNote: Commands come from Headroom's README. AIRepoHub hasn't run them yet.

steps.title: Compress messages before calling the model
steps.code:
from headroom import compress
result = compress(messages, model="gpt-4o")
client.chat.completions.create(model="gpt-4o", messages=result.messages)

steps.title: Install the SDK and the proxy
steps.body: The npm SDK sends messages to the proxy.
steps.code:
npm install headroom-ai
pip install "headroom-ai[proxy]"
headroom proxy --port 8787

environment.name: HEADROOM_OFFLINE
environment.description: Set to 1 for a run with no network access.

firstRun.title: Watch savings live (proxy must be running)

tutorial.title: Compress messages in your own Python app
tutorial.useCase: Cut input tokens before calling the OpenAI API.

steps.title: Compress, call and report savings
steps.code:
from headroom import compress
from openai import OpenAI

messages = [{"role": "user", "content": "Analyze these results"}]
result = compress(messages, model="gpt-4o")
client = OpenAI()
response = client.chat.completions.create(model="gpt-4o", messages=result.messages)
print(f"Saved {result.tokens_saved} tokens ({result.compression_ratio:.0%})")

tutorial.expected: The request goes through with compressed messages and the script prints how many tokens were saved. User messages are left alone unless you pass compress_user_messages=True.

troubleshooting.solution: Run headroom doctor to confirm requests go through Headroom.

troubleshooting.problem: The proxy stops when the agent exits
troubleshooting.solution: headroom wrap is session-scoped; use headroom deploy for a proxy that survives reboots.

troubleshooting.problem: Want to remove it from an agent
troubleshooting.solution: Run headroom unwrap followed by the tool name, for example headroom unwrap claude.
That is the default; pass compress_user_messages=True to include them.

bestFor: Coding agents with heavy tool output
